title: ‘Here be giants’ – unlocking Africa’s deepwater exploration puzzle | Wood Mackenzie
gist: Wood Mackenzie says the African Atlantic Margin is the world's hottest exploration play: >50% success rates, virtually all of Africa's 17.3 bn boe discovered in 2016-2025, and a Majors' land grab of 630,000 km2 in five years. Eni's fast-tracked Baleine and TotalEnergies' complex Venus (FID imminent) illustrate both the prize and the subsurface risk, with explorers warned to expect a humbling experience.

themes.theme: Big Oil's return to high-impact exploration

insights.claim: Big Oil is doubling down on high-impact exploration after a decade of capital discipline and improved value creation helped regain investor support for exploration investment.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Exploration capex is back in favour with investors, supporting upstream spend and frontier-acreage deals.
insights.quote: Big Oil is doubling down on high-impact exploration.
insights.locator: Big Oil is doubling down on

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie argues exploration can deliver advantaged barrels to meet stronger-for-longer oil and gas demand, underpinning the renewed exploration push.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: A 'stronger-for-longer' demand view justifies long-cycle deepwater projects that pay out over decades.
insights.quote: exploration can deliver advantaged barrels to meet stronger-for-longer oil and gas demand
insights.locator: Big Oil is doubling down on

insights.claim: War in the Gulf has added a supply-diversification motive to exploration, raising the value of non-Gulf sources such as West Africa's Atlantic margin.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Geopolitical risk premia on Gulf supply increase the strategic value of Atlantic-basin barrels.
insights.quote: War in the Gulf has added another dimension – the market’s need for diverse sources of supply.
insights.locator: Big Oil is doubling down on

insights.claim: For a decade, the African Atlantic margin has led the world in exploration success rates (above 50%), volumes discovered per well, and average discovery size.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Best-in-class geological risk/reward explains why the Majors are concentrating frontier capital here.
insights.quote: exploration success rates (more than 50%), volumes discovered per well (well above than the next best)

insights.claim: Virtually all of the 17.3 billion boe discovered on the African continent between 2016 and 2025 was on the Atlantic Margin.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: African resource growth is essentially an Atlantic Margin story; East/North Africa exploration is marginal by comparison.
insights.quote: Virtually all of the 17.3 billion boe discovered between 2016 and 2025 on the African continent have been on the Atlantic Margin.

insights.claim: Giant discoveries over the past five years have opened new basins and new plays in mature producing basins, lifting perceptions of the margin's potential.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: New-play discoveries in mature basins can extend the life of existing producing countries' fiscal and infrastructure bases.

insights.claim: Eni's 2021 Baleine discovery offshore Cote d'Ivoire, in 1,200m of water in a high-quality Cretaceous carbonate, holds initial recoverable reserves of 0.75 billion bbls of oil and 1.0 Tcf gas.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: A shallow-ish, high-quality reservoir is the low-risk template for fast monetisation on the margin.
insights.quote: in 1,200 metres water depth, in a high-quality Cretaceous carbonate

insights.claim: Eni brought Baleine into production within two years of discovery and it is heading to a 180,000 boe/d peak in 2030.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Eni's fast-track discovery-to-production model compresses payback and is a differentiator versus peers.
insights.quote: In true Eni-style, the project was in production inside two years, on its way to peak at 180,000 boe/d in 2030.

insights.claim: TotalEnergies' 2022 Venus discovery offshore Namibia sits in 3,000m of water in a complex Cretaceous turbidite reservoir with low permeability and a high gas ratio, despite being among Africa's biggest finds ever.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Big in-place volumes do not equal easy barrels; reservoir quality drives development cost and recovery.
insights.quote: the reservoir is highly complex with low permeability and has a high gas ratio

insights.claim: FID on TotalEnergies' Venus project in Namibia is anticipated imminently, targeting recovery of 0.75 billion bbls of oil.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Venus FID is a near-term catalyst for TotalEnergies and for Namibia's emergence as a producer.
insights.quote: FID is anticipated imminently for a project expected to recover 0.75 billion bbls of oil.

insights.claim: The contrast between Baleine and Venus - scale, commerciality and very different geology - explains both the renewed enthusiasm for the Atlantic Margin and the challenges explorers will face.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Investors should differentiate margin assets by reservoir quality and water depth, not headline volumes.
insights.quote: But they also highlight the challenges that are likely to be encountered.

insights.claim: The Majors have captured 630,000 km2 of acreage around Africa in the past five years, much of it on the Atlantic Margin, over three times as much as in either Asia or Latin America/Caribbean.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Portfolio positioning implies Africa will dominate Majors' frontier drilling programmes for years.
insights.quote: an astonishing land grab is underway down the entire Atlantic coast

insights.claim: Governments are increasingly awarding MOUs or 'reconnaissance' permits with low or minimal drilling commitments alongside traditional PSCs and concessions, to encourage acreage uptake.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Low-commitment entry lets Majors take cheap options on huge areas, shifting host-government bargaining power toward oil companies.

insights.claim: Non-producing countries such as Morocco, Guinea, Sierra Leone, Liberia and Guinea-Bissau are also using low-commitment permits to attract explorers in a super-competitive market for capital.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Competition among host states for exploration capital favours explorers on fiscal terms.
insights.quote: to attract explorers in what is a super-competitive market

insights.claim: Sierra Leone and Liberia, abandoned by explorers after disappointing wells decades ago, are now welcoming explorers back on the strength of wildcat successes in Namibia and Cote d'Ivoire.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Re-opened frontier basins offer option value but carry a history of dry holes.

insights.claim: The Atlantic Margin is vast enough to hold multiple Guyanas, where ExxonMobil has discovered 9 billion bbls of recoverable oil since 2015.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: The upside case is several Guyana-scale plays, which would reshape non-OPEC supply growth.

insights.claim: Very few wells drilled in the Atlantic Margin's new plays have come in as expected, as subsurface understanding is still being pieced together.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Expect high variance in well outcomes; the land grab raises the risk of expensive dry holes and write-offs.
insights.quote: very few wells drilled in the new plays have come in as expected

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie warns that explorers entering the Atlantic Margin should be prepared for a humbling experience despite the bullish acreage grab.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Tempers the bull case: exploration write-downs are likely to accompany the few giant wins.
insights.quote: should be prepared for a humbling experience
